There could be an opportunity for both Corum and Williams to succeed against a Cardinals defense that is giving up 99.6 rushing yards per game to RBs, ranking 19th in the league.

roster.name: KC Concepcion
roster.outlook: In Week 10, KC Concepcion and the Browns are home for the first time since Week 6 to host the Texans. He grabbed four of six targets for 85 yards, including a 64-yard touchdown, during Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss in Week 9. The score was the rookie wideout's first of his young career, and he now sports a 37-437-1 receiving line on 55 targets to go along with 10 carries for 37 yards through nine games. Concepcion will aim to take advantage of a Houston defense allowing the third-most fantasy points per game (38.5) to opposing WRs.

roster.name: Keenan Allen
roster.outlook: Keenan Allen led the Colts with 40 catches on 58 targets, and his 351 receiving yards were just three shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total, with Allen having played one fewer game. Both players were shipped out of Indianapolis at the trade deadline however, with Allen landing with a San Francisco team in dire need of wide receiver depth. If the veteran gets up to speed on Kyle Shanahan's playbook quickly, he could find himself as Brock Purdy's No. 1 WR in Week 10 against a Cowboys secondary that is tied for 25th in fantasy points were game allowed to wideouts, although Allen could also be as low as No. 3 on the chart chart if Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel are both able to return from their respective injuries.

roster.name: Bam Knight
roster.outlook: Bam Knight will look to clear concussion protocol in time to play in Arizona's Week 10 matchup against the Rams. Knight missed the team's Week 9 loss to Seattle after being concussed Week 8. If he's able to play against Los Angeles, Knight could have a prominent role in the backfield beside Tyler Allgeier, as Jeremiyah Love is on IR due to an ankle injury. However, the Cardinals' backfield as a whole faces a tough test against a Rams defense that is yielding just 3.55 yards per carry to running backs, fourth-best in the NFL.

roster.name: Chad Ryland
roster.outlook: Chad Ryland's opportunities could be influenced by a new Cardinals' starting quarterback (Carson Beck) against the Rams in Week 10. Arizona is coming off a battle against a top defensive unit, and Ryland got just one chance to kick -- making a short field goal -- in Week 9 against Seattle. Gardner Minshew suffered an elbow injury in that contest, leading the rookie Beck to presumably make his NFL debut as the starting QB against the Rams. Perhaps Ryland will get multiple field-goal opportunities against a Los Angeles defense that has allowed the most FG tries (26) in the NFL this season.

roster.name: Ryan Flournoy
roster.outlook: Ryan Flournoy could not take advantage of the absence of George Pickens last game for Dallas. Despite Pickens being sidelined with a hamstring issue, Flournoy managed his fewest catches since Week 3. He finished with just two grabs for the contest, though did gain 53 yards total on the receptions. While Pickens may be shelved for Week 10 as well, Flournoy will face a difficult task versus the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.

roster.name: Brenton Strange
roster.outlook: Brenton Strange is a viable fantasy option in Week 10 against the Titans, but he's far from a must-start. He leads the Jaguars with 30 catches through eight games but hasn't scored since the season opener and is averaging 45 yards per game, which ranks 10th among TEs. Tennessee has struggled to defend the pass in general, but the Titans have limited TEs to 43 yards per game, though they have also given up four TDs to the position through eight games.

roster.name: Bijan Robinson
roster.outlook: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of the Falcons' offense in the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. Robinson was one of Atlanta's few bright spots during the Week 9 loss to the Bengals, accumulating 147 yards and a touchdown on 25 touches. The Texas product is currently averaging the third-most touches per game (22.2) in the NFL, suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top running backs despite a tough matchup. Kansas City's defense has given up just 20.1 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs through eight games this year.

roster.name: Drake London
roster.outlook: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top pass catcher during the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. London has cooled down after a terrific stretch of games from Weeks 3 through 5, averaging just 4.3 receptions and 52.8 receiving yards per game over Atlanta's last four contests. He's also averaging just 7.6 targets per game this season, his lowest mark since 2023, so it appears the Falcons are struggling to get him involved. Additionally, London is in for a difficult Week 10 matchup against a Chiefs secondary that's allowed just 23.5 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.

roster.name: Nico Collins
roster.outlook: Nico Collins has shared the wealth in recent weeks as the locked-in C.J. Stroud spreads the ball around to a deep Texans WR room that also includes Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison and Kayshon Boutte. Collins has been targeted five or fewer times in each of the past three games, scoring just once over that span while averaging three catches for 45 yards. He'll need to pick up the pace to reach the 1,000-yard receiving mark for a fourth consecutive season. Collins has dropped from his customary fantasy WR1 standing to the WR2 range for a Week 10 matchup with a Browns secondary that's allowing 144 yards per game to WRs.

roster.name: Tyler Warren
roster.outlook: Tyler Warren has drawn at least seven targets in five of his last six appearances. The 2025 first-round pick remains a weekly fantasy starter at TE thanks to his hefty volume, even though he's averaging just 5.2 yards per target in the Colts' low-octane passing offense. Warren and the Colts will face a Dolphins defense in Week 10 that has allowed six receiving TDs in eight games to TEs. In addition to two touchdown catches, Warren has one rushing score this season.

roster.name: DK Metcalf
roster.outlook: DK Metcalf and the Steelers travel to Cincinnati for a divisional clash in Week 10. He caught just one of six targets for four yards during Pittsburgh's 27-6 victory in Week 8, giving the 28-year-old a 3-60-0 receiving line on 12 targets over his last two contests. Metcalf and the Steelers didn't have to throw much while playing most of Week 8 with a double-digit advantage, but that could change in Week 10 versus a high-powered Bengals offense on Sunday Night Football. In his first matchup against Cincinnati, Metcalf corralled three of five targets for 31 yards and his only TD of the season.

roster.name: Rachaad White
roster.outlook: Rachaad White continues to operate as the top back for the Commanders, though has found little room to roam on the ground. White has failed to rush for more than 55 yards in any game this season. However, he does have at least two receptions in three-straight contests. In Week 10, White will face a Giants defense that has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL. However, the Giants are surrendering 123.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the league.

roster.name: Jordan Addison
roster.outlook: Jordan Addison will look to get more volume in Week 10 as the Vikings play the Packers. Addison finished a Week 9 loss with two catches for 28 yards off three targets, but struggles from the QB room didn't leave much room for any pass catchers to succeed. The trade deadline acquisition of Kirk Cousins to be Minnesota's new starting quarterback could be just the spark Addison needs, as he's recorded less than 30 yards in two of his last three games. Green Bay has ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.

roster.name: Dalton Kincaid
roster.outlook: Dalton Kincaid's role in the Bills offense may be sliding as they enter a Week 10 matchup against the Jets. In Buffalo's first six games, Kincaid garnered less than a 66% snap share just once, but since the team's Week 7 bye, he's been under 60% in two outings, resulting in just nine targets. The Jets have been vulnerable against tight ends, allowing at least 72 yards in three straight weeks, but Kincaid's recent workload is a concern.

roster.name: Jason Myers
roster.outlook: Jason Myers will hope for more kicking opportunities when Seattle faces Las Vegas in Week 10. Myers made his lone field goal and both his extra-point tries in Week 9 against Arizona as the Seahawks scored fewer than 21 points for the fourth straight week. The veteran kicker has been good when called upon this season, though, making 16 of 18 FG tries through nine games. He could be more active against the Raiders, who are giving up a league-worst 29.8 points per game.

roster.name: T.J. Hockenson
roster.outlook: T.J. Hockenson should remain a top option in Minnesota's passing game versus the Packers in Week 10. Hockenson led the Vikings in catches in a Week 9 loss to the Bills, which was a quiet four grabs for 33 yards. The veteran tight end has now reeled in four receptions in each of the last three weeks. The addition of Kirk Cousins at the trade deadline to be the new starting QB may not be good news for Hockenson, however, as he's more likely to targets wideouts Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison than Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz did. Hockenson will face a Green Bay defense that he posted a 4-36-1 receiving line against in Week 1, and which ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Jordan Love
roster.outlook: Jordan Love will look to keep his MVP campaign rolling as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Love was on fire again in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, completing 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards with three passing touchdowns and a 13-yard rushing score. Green Bay's signal caller has now dished out two or more touchdowns and passed for 270 or more yards in each of his last three outings. He'll rematch a Vikings defense that he threw for 387 yards, two touchdowns and one interception against in a Week 1 loss.

free_agents.name: Kirk Cousins
free_agents.outlook: Kirk Cousins is coming off his worst performance of the season, getting picked off three times while throwing just one touchdown in the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers. With Las Vegas now 4-5, the team elected to hand the reins of the offense to rookie Fernando Mendoza by trading Cousins back to the franchise he had the most success with, the Vikings. Cousins' 20 TD passes through nine games is second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow's 23, and he's fifth in passing yards. Given his familiarity with Kevin O'Connell's offense, he should immediately step in as the starter for Minnesota in Week 10 against a Packers defense that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Marvin Harrison accounted for just 20 of C.J. Stroud's 384 passing yards and none of Stroud's five touchdown passes in Houston's Week 9 win over the Chargers. The trade acquisition from Arizona has just six catches for 60 yards and one TD in three appearances for Houston heading into a Week 10 trip to Cleveland. With Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte also vying for targets in Houston's deep WR room, Harrison isn't a trustworthy Week 10 fantasy option. The 2024 fourth overall pick is droppable in most redraft formats, as the change of scenery hasn't improved Harrison's short-term fantasy outlook.

free_agents.name: Harrison Butker
free_agents.outlook: Harrison Butker missed another field goal in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, but he converted all five of his extra points. The veteran kicker has an awful 63.2% success rate on field goal attempts through eight games, going just 12-for-19 including a weak 2-for-8 showing from 50-plus yards, but so far Andy Reid has stuck with him. Butker will try to regain some confidence indoors in a Week 10 road trip to Atlanta against a Falcons team that's given up 24.8 points per game this season, tied for 20th in the league.

free_agents.name: Devaughn Vele
free_agents.outlook: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain one of New Orleans' top wideouts during the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. With the debut of 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson in the Week 9 overtime win over the Browns, Vele caught just two of four targets for 17 yards, which are all season-lows in a single game. Even with Tyson on the field, Vele should remain a valuable part of the Saints' offense, but he likely won't be as consistent for fantasy purposes for the remainder of the year. Vele could still be productive in Week 10 against an injury-riddled Carolina secondary that's allowed 7.4 yards per target to opposing wideouts this season.

free_agents.name: Dominic Zvada
free_agents.outlook: Dominic Zvada rebounded last game for the Giants with four field goals. Zvada did not miss a boot, connecting from at least 48 yards on three of his four field goal tries. He also added an extra points in the 19-11 win over the Eagles. He should have plenty more opportunities to score in Week 10 versus a lackluster Washington squad. The Commanders are allowing 25.3 points per game, which is 24th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Cameron Dicker
free_agents.outlook: Cameron Dicker continues to benefit from the Chargers' inability to finish drives. The 26-year-old kicker has booted multiple field goals in five of the last six games, going 15-for-16 on FG attempts over that stretch but attempting just six extra points, converting them all. The steady volume gives Dicker a solid floor heading into a Week 10 clash with a Ravens team allowing 26.2 points per game, tied for 25th in the league.

free_agents.name: Aaron Rodgers
free_agents.outlook: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers are in Cincinnati for a Week 10 showdown on Sunday Night Football. In a Week 8 victory over Cleveland, he threw for 172 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, snapping a five-game streak of at least one TD pass. Pittsburgh relied on its ground game in that win, rushing 33 times compared to just 25 pass attempts. Rodgers will have to throw more in order to keep pace with the high-scoring Bengals' offense. He'll try to repeat his Week 3 performance when he threw for 292 yards with three TDs and one INT during the Steelers' first matchup with their division rival.

free_agents.name: Eddy Pineiro
free_agents.outlook: Eddy Pineiro hasn't had many chances for field goals of late ahead of San Francisco's Week 10 matchup against Dallas. Pineiro make his only FG attempt this past Sunday against the Raiders and has now attempted one or zero field goals in five of eight games this season. That's largely because the 49ers' offense has been so effective -- they have 22 TDs and just four FGs in 26 trips to the red zone. It could be more of the same for Pineiro against the Cowboys, who have allowed 27 PAT tries and 17 FG attempts this season.

free_agents.name: Justin Herbert
free_agents.outlook: Justin Herbert is coming off another shaky performance in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, completing fewer than 60% of his pass attempts and throwing his league-leading 11th interception of the season. The 28-year-old quarterback has yet to throw multiple TDs in any game this season, as the addition of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel has been a complete disaster for the Chargers. He also emerged from the loss to Houston with a finger injury on his non-throwing hand. The issue doesn't seem likely to cost him any time, however. Herbert will try to begin righting the ship in Week 10 against a Ravens defense that's tied for 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: J.J. McCarthy
free_agents.outlook: J.J. McCarthy is battling a hip pointer, but should be able to suit up in Week 10 for the Giants versus the Commanders. McCarthy briefly left New York's last contest versus the Eagles due to the issue, but was able to return and ultimately guide the G-Men to victory. Though McCarthy passed for a season-low 127 yards last game, he will look to rebound against a porous Washington secondary. The Commanders are allowing 240 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, Washington has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 25th in the league.

free_agents.name: Travis Hunter
free_agents.outlook: Travis Hunter has just one fantasy-relevant performance on offense this season while playing much more cornerback than wide receiver for the Jaguars. The 2025 second overall pick has the talent to thrive if injuries and/or roster moves open up more opportunities on offense, but Hunter can't be trusted as a starter outside of individual defensive player formats as things stand. Expect Hunter to play just a few snaps on offense as usual in Week 10, which won't give him many chances to capitalize on facing Tennessee's generous secondary.

free_agents.name: Mack Hollins
free_agents.outlook: Mack Hollins' opportunities for the Patriots in Week 10 against the Lions appear unsettled with A.J. Brown (knee) potentially returning to action. Hollins returned from a four-week absence in Week 9, catching half of his six targets and finding the end zone for the first time all season. While Detroit's secondary has been picked on often and allows 8.0 yards per target, Hollins doesn't have a clear path to heavy volume, leading to big-play or touchdown dependency.

free_agents.name: Evan McPherson
free_agents.outlook: Evan McPherson and the Bengals battle the Steelers for an AFC North showdown in Week 10. He went 2-for-2 on field goals and made all four of his PATs during Cincinnati's 34-17 victory in Week 9. McPherson is one of two kickers who are still perfect at this point in the season, and he'll look to keep that going versus a Pittsburgh defense allowing just 18.0 points per game, tied for the fourth fewest.

free_agents.name: Mike Gesicki
free_agents.outlook: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals host the Steelers for an AFC North clash in Week 10. He corralled both of his targets for 11 yards during Cincinnati's 34-17 victory in Week 9. Gesicki's five-game streak with a touchdown came to an end with all three of Joe Burrow's TD passes going to Ja'Marr Chase (one) and Tee Higgins (two). Gesicki's fantasy value has been reliant on TDs in 2026, so he'll try to start another streak of consecutive trips to the endzone versus a Pittsburgh defense his initial scoring stretch started against back in Week 3.

free_agents.name: Quentin Johnston
free_agents.outlook: Quentin Johnston caught his first touchdown of the season in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, but it was also his only catch of the contest on four targets. The fourth-year wide receiver has hauled in more than two passes just twice in seven appearances this season, scratching out a 13-260-1 line on 30 targets. He's generally failed to take advantage of Ladd McConkey's frequent absences in one of the NFL's most dysfunctional offenses. Johnston is unlikely to suddenly break out in Week 10, even against a Ravens secondary that's tied for 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Sam Darnold
free_agents.outlook: Sam Darnold is slated to miss Seattle's Week 10 matchup against Las Vegas due to a quadriceps injury. Drew Lock is dealing with an oblique issue but is expected to be able to start at quarterback for a second straight week.

free_agents.name: Dalton Schultz
free_agents.outlook: Dalton Schultz is a borderline fantasy starter at TE for Week 10 against the Browns. He ranks ninth among TEs with 46 receiving yards per game but has yet to score this season and has a meager five TDs in 42 regular-season appearances since the start of the 2024 season. Cleveland has allowed five TDs to the position in nine games, as well as 58 yards per game.

free_agents.name: Rashid Shaheed
free_agents.outlook: Rashid Shaheed (knee) has missed Seattle's past two games and isn't certain to return in Week 10 against the Raiders. Shaheed hasn't practiced since getting hurt in Week 7, and he'll likely need to return to at least a few limited sessions before being ready to play in games again. Should Shaheed sit out another contest, Cooper Kupp and Tory Horton will likely continue to be the Seahawks' top wideouts behind superstar Jaxon Smith-Njigba. If Shaheed can suit up, though, he'll face a Raiders defense that has allowed 27 passing plays of 20-plus yards this season, tied for eighth-most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Tyjae Spears
free_agents.outlook: Tyjae Spears hasn't suited up since Week 6 due to a knee injury and has also dealt with an ankle injury this season. Even if he returns to his customary change-of-pace role for the Titans in Week 10, Spears is unlikely to contribute much against a Jacksonville defense that has been elite at containing RBs. If the Titans trade lead back Tony Pollard, Spears could see an uptick in work, but the biggest beneficiary in that scenario would likely be rookie fifth-round pick Nicholas Singleton.

free_agents.name: Michael Mayer
free_agents.outlook: Michael Mayer posted modest numbers in the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers, catching all three of his targets for 37 yards. The fourth-year tight end has snagged at least three passes in eight of nine games this season, and he's already set new career highs with 39 receptions and 388 receiving yards. Even with Brock Bowers ahead of him on the depth chart, Mayer's role is large enough to give him some value heading into a Week 10 clash with a Seahawks defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

free_agents.name: Keon Coleman
free_agents.outlook: Keon Coleman continues to struggle for meaningful action as the Bills prepare to face the Jets in Week 10. Coleman drew six targets in Week 9, the second time he's done so in three games, but finished with only 17 yards, the fourth time he's been limited to under 20 yards. With DJ Moore healthy, Coleman is at best the third option in Buffalo's passing game, and facing a defense that's allowed just nine touchdown receptions to wideouts in as many outings doesn't give Coleman much of a ceiling.

free_agents.name: Fernando Mendoza
free_agents.outlook: Fernando Mendoza will take over under center in Week 10 with the Raiders dealing Kirk Cousins to the Vikings for a 2027 third-round pick. Mendoza has only appeared once this season, playing during garbage time of a Week 5 loss to the Patriots. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft was not impressive during camp but has looked solid in recent practices. His first game as a starter will come against the stout Seahawks defense. It won't get any easier in Week 11 versus the Broncos, so it's best to take the wait-and-see approach before trusting the rookie for fantasy production.

free_agents.name: Jayden Reed
free_agents.outlook: Jayden Reed will remain inactive as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, which requires season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

free_agents.name: Drew Lock
free_agents.outlook: Drew Lock  is expected to start for Seattle in Week 10 against Las Vegas despite managing an oblique injury. It will be the second straight start for Lock, as Sam Darnold is slated to sit out again due to a quad injury. Lock led the Seahawks to a win this past Sunday against the Cardinals but put up modest numbers, throwing for 175 yards and one touchdown with no interceptions. He'll have a good matchup against the Raiders, who have allowed a 103.6 QB rating to passers this season, fourth-worst in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jacoby Brissett
free_agents.outlook: Jacoby Brissett and the Ravens host the Chargers on Monday Night Football in Week 10. After being acquired via trade from the Cardinals, Brissett is expected to earn his first start for Baltimore. In eight outings with Arizona, he completed 193 of 305 pass attempts (63.3%) for 1,719 yards with a 10:7 TD:INT ratio, to go along with 29 carries for 87 yards and one score. The Ravens desperately need Brissett's veteran presence under center with Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) both on IR. Baltimore has scored exactly 10 points in three of their last four games, with their best mark being 13 points in a loss to the Bengals in Week 7. Brissett will get a favorable matchup versus a Chargers defense allowing 27.4 points per contest, tied for the fourth-most in the league.

free_agents.name: Jason Sanders
free_agents.outlook: Jason Sanders brings a high ceiling into the Jets' Week 10 game against the Bills. He has attempted at least four field goals in consecutive games and three of his last four, with the Jets' offense failing to convert drives into touchdowns, evident by just six PATs over this four-game stretch. Buffalo is allowing the eighth-fewest fantasy points to opposing kickers, and field goals aren't likely to help the Jets in Week 10, but Sanders' recent run of scoring puts him in the streaming mix.

free_agents.name: Tutu Atwell
free_agents.outlook: Tutu Atwell will have a chance to step into a larger role for the Rams in Week 10 against Arizona. Atwell has logged a modest four catches for 68 yards on nine targets over his past two games after going catchless in Week 7. However, Puka Nacua is expected to land on IR due to a knee injury, so the Rams are going to need to look to other wideouts, potentially including Atwell, to step up in the passing game. A matchup against the Cardinals presents a good opportunity, as they rank 24th in the NFL with 22.2 fantasy points per game allowed to wide receivers.

free_agents.name: Michael Penix Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Michael Penix will lead the Falcons' offense into the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. Penix has underwhelmed over Atlanta's last two games, completing just 28 of 55 pass attempts for 287 yards, one touchdown and five interceptions. This is especially disappointing considering Penix's terrific start to the year, in which he averaged 231.4 passing yards and 1.8 passing touchdowns per game, while turning the ball over just twice over his first five appearances. Penix's struggles will likely continue in Week 10, as he's set to face a Kansas City defense that's given up just 16.1 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, the third-fewest in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Justice Hill
free_agents.outlook: Justice Hill and the Ravens host the winless Chargers on Monday Night Football in Week 10. He erupted for 85 yards on nine carries, including a 65-yard TD run, and caught all three of his targets for seven yards during Baltimore's Week 9 loss. With Jacoby Brissett expected to start under center, Hill and the Ravens' offense could start to become a bit more pass-friendly, but that's certainly no guarantee. He'll look to keep contributing against the Chargers' 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (22.8) to opposing RBs.

free_agents.name: Kimani Vidal
free_agents.outlook: Kimani Vidal remains stuck in a committee in the Chargers' backfield. While Vidal turned eight touches into 36 scrimmage yards in a Week 9 loss to the Texans, Omarion Hampton gained a team-high 60 rushing yards on 13 carries, and Keaton Mitchell put together 67 scrimmage yards on 10 touches. That leaves Vidal dependent on TDs or injuries around him on the depth chart for value. He'll try to make a splash in Week 10 against a Ravens defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Daniel Jones
free_agents.outlook: Daniel Jones is staying in Indianapolis after the trade deadline, though it's fair to wonder how long the 2-7 Colts will stick with the struggling veteran over younger options Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard. Jones hasn't produced a multi-TD performance all season, and that drought seems unlikely to conclude in Week 10 against a Dolphins defense that has been better recently and just held Detroit's Jared Goff without a TD in Week 9. These two teams have combined for just three wins, so there are more draft implications than fantasy implications in this Week 10 matchup. Even in superflex and multi-QB formats, Jones is best avoided.

free_agents.name: Deshaun Watson
free_agents.outlook: Deshaun Watson and the Browns welcome his former team to town when they host the Texans in Week 10. He was inactive for Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss in Week 9 due to a concussion sustained in Week 8's loss. Shedeur Sanders earned his first start of the season, but Watson is healthy and expected to retain his role as the starting QB versus Houston. He'll battle a Texans defense allowing 21.8 fantasy points per game (25th) to the position.

free_agents.name: AJ Barner
free_agents.outlook: AJ Barner will look to build upon his two-touchdown game when Seattle visits Las Vegas in Week 10. Barner had one score through the air and another on the ground in a Week 9 win over Arizona.  Though his receiving output has remained modest, Barner has been getting more opportunities to carry the ball in short-yardage situations in recent weeks, as he's logged six carries over his past three games. He'll seek to get into the end zone against the Raiders, who have given up the second-most TDs (eight) to tight ends this season.

free_agents.name: Konata Mumpfield
free_agents.outlook: Konata Mumpfield may need to step up for the Rams in Week 10 against the Cardinals. Mumpfield has been quiet of late, logging no more than two catches and 20 yards over his past six games. However, with Davante Adams (hamstring) on IR and Puka Nacua (knee) expected to join him there, Los Angeles is likely going to need some of its other wideouts to start being more productive. Mumpfield has a good matchup against Arizona, as the Cardinals have given up 11 receiving TDs to wideouts, tied for second-most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Tyler Higbee
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Higbee may need to ramp up his production for the Rams' passing game to be successful, beginning with a Week 10 matchup in Arizona. Higbee continued his recent trend of limited production this past Sunday against Washington, logging just one catch for 13 yards on five targets. He's recorded two or fewer receptions in three straight games, but Los Angeles may need Higbee to be more impactful after losing star WR Puka Nacua for what is likely to be multiple weeks due to a knee injury. The Cardinals rank 27th in the NFL with 10.4 fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends this season.

free_agents.name: Malik Willis
free_agents.outlook: Malik Willis is headed for the IR after an MRI revealed a core-muscle injury. The diagnosis will sideline him through at least Week 13. Kyle McCord is poised to take over under center.

free_agents.name: Malachi Fields
free_agents.outlook: Malachi Fields has at least five targets in each of the last three games for the Giants. Unfortunately, he has gained more than 40 yards receiving in just one of those three outings. In Week 10, he will look to take advantage of a porous Washington secondary. The Commanders are allowing 240 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, Washington has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 25th in the league.

free_agents.name: Samaje Perine
free_agents.outlook: Samaje Perine and the Bengals host the Steelers on Sunday Night Football in Week 10. He rushed 11 times for 43 yards and was not targeted during Cincinnati's 34-17 victory in Week 9. Perine played 42% of the offensive snaps compared to 62% for Chase Brown, although their workloads were much closer, with the latter out-touching the former 12-11. As it stands, with the Bengals lighting up opponents through the air, fantasy managers should find it difficult to trust either running back.

free_agents.name: Eli Raridon
free_agents.outlook: Eli Raridon is trending favorably ahead of the Patriots' Week 10 matchup against a Lions defense that struggles against tight ends. Raridon has collected at least four targets in three straight games, even with fellow tight end Hunter Henry healthy, and the Lions are allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends. While still a secondary option in New England's passing game, Raridon can garner enough attention to be a viable option in a plus matchup.

free_agents.name: Cooper Kupp
free_agents.outlook: Cooper Kupp continues to be quiet this season ahead of Seattle's Week 10 visit to Las Vegas. Kupp logged a 3-32-0 receiving line this past Sunday against Arizona despite Rashid Shaheed (knee) continuing to be sidelined. Kupp's four targets in the game were actually his third-most through nine games, emphasizing how little attention he's gotten from the Seahawks' quarterbacks this season. With that said, he at least has a good matchup coming up, as the Raiders have given up 11 receiving TDs to wideouts this season -- tied for second-most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Rashod Bateman
free_agents.outlook: In Week 10, Rashod Bateman and the Ravens host a Chargers defense allowing 36.9 fantasy points per game (27th) to WRs. He caught one of two targets for six yards during Baltimore's Week 9 loss. Bateman now has one or fewer receptions in three of his last four outings, tallying a 4-55-0 line on 10 targets over that stretch. He'll have the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett starting under center, but Bateman should be left on fantasy benches until proven otherwise.

free_agents.name: Treylon Burks
free_agents.outlook: Treylon Burks did not play last game for the Commanders due to a foot injury. In his place, Van Jefferson was the surprise leading receiver, snagging a team-high 58 yards and a touchdown in the 20-13 loss to Washington. Even if Burks can return in Week 10, he will face a difficult test in the form of the New York Giants. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Andre Szmyt
free_agents.outlook: In Week 10, Andre Szmyt and the Browns return home for the first time since Week 6 to host the 3-5 Texans. He made all three of his field goal attempts and his lone PAT during Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss in Week 9. Szmyt has at least two FGAs in every outing since the season opener, providing a solid fantasy floor despite playing for one of the worst offenses in the league. He'll aim to have a repeat performance against the Steelers, when the 28-year-old went 5-for-5 on kicks, including a game-winning 56-yarder, back in Week 4.

free_agents.name: Austin Ekeler
free_agents.outlook: Austin Ekeler had a season-high 10 touches last game for Washington. Unfortunately, he managed just 34 yards with those opportunities, and the Commanders fell to the Rams by a score of 20-13. Ekeler has 16 carries over the last two contests, though continues to serve as the backup to Rachaad White. In Week 10, Ekeler will face a Giants defense that has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL. However, the Giants are surrendering 123.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the league.

free_agents.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Fitzgerald is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Panthers' Week 10 matchup against the Saints. Fitzgerald missed his first field goal of the season during the Week 9 loss to the Broncos but converted on all three extra points. Through eight games this year, Fitzgerald has made 13 of 14 field-goal attempts but just 16 of 21 point-after tries. He's expected to have lots of scoring chances against the Saints in Week 10, as New Orleans has allowed 8.8 kicking points per game this season.

free_agents.name: Mason Taylor
free_agents.outlook: Mason Taylor is trending in the wrong direction ahead of the Jets' Week 10 matchup with the Bills. After a Week 7 flash, scoring twice on five receptions, Taylor has only four catches and 30 yards over the subsequent two weeks. While the Jets will likely throw at least 30 times in Week 10 for the sixth straight game, Buffalo has allowed only one tight end to score, which could limit Taylor's ceiling.

free_agents.name: Darnell Washington
free_agents.outlook: In Week 10, Darnell Washington and the Steelers are on the road for a divisional clash against the Bengals. He caught three of five targets for 94 yards during Pittsburgh's 27-6 victory in Week 8. Washington led the team in yardage while finishing second in receptions and tied for second in targets. The 94 receiving yards marked a new season high, as he now boasts a 19-254-3 line on 28 targets through eight outings. Washington will attempt to take advantage of a Cincinnati defense allowing 15.5 fantasy points per game to TEs, which ranks 24th.

free_agents.name: Cam Ward
free_agents.outlook: Cam Ward had his best game of the season in Tennessee's 43-36 Week 8 loss to the Bengals, prior to a Week 9 bye. He threw for 300 yards for the first time in his career and delivered a pair of touchdown passes for his first multi-TD performance through the air all season. Ward has a chance to build on that effort in Week 10 against a Jaguars defense that has been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground. The far larger sample of subpar football from the 2025 first overall pick prior to his strong outing last game suggests Ward remains tough to trust for now, even in superflex formats. The Jaguars are giving up the 11th-most passing yards per game, though they have more interceptions (11) than touchdown passes allowed (eight).

free_agents.name: Colby Parkinson
free_agents.outlook: Colby Parkinson could be a big part of the Rams' passing game in Week 10 against Arizona. Parkinson ranked second on Los Angeles with four catches against Washington this past Sunday, though he gained just 13 yards on those receptions. Still, the Rams are going to need some pass catchers to step up in the wake of a knee injury that is likely going to cause star wideout Puka Nacua to miss multiple games, and Parkinson has tallied at least four catches in each of the last three games in which he's played. The Cardinals have struggled against tight ends, giving up six receiving touchdowns, tied for sixth-most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jahan Dotson
free_agents.outlook: Jahan Dotson is expected to remain Atlanta's No. 2 wideout in the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. Dotson was ineffective during the Week 9 loss to the Bengals, catching both of his targets for 16 yards. Despite this, he tied his season-high in snap share, playing 85% of the Falcons' offensive snaps, which suggests he's firmly ahead of Olamide Zaccheaus in the team's receiving corps. Dotson will likely still struggle in Week 10 against a tough Kansas City secondary that's allowed just 6.5 yards per target to opposing wide receivers this year.

free_agents.name: Xavier Hutchinson
free_agents.outlook: Xavier Hutchinson takes a two-game touchdown streak into Houston's Week 10 road game against the Browns, but he has just 46 receiving yards over that span and is averaging a meager 36 receiving yards per game this season. He has maintained a prominent role in a high-ceiling Houston passing offense, drawing at least five targets in all but one game, but Hutchinson hasn't done much with those opportunities and had just three career TDs in 3.5 seasons prior to his current two-game scoring streak. Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison, and Kayshon Boutte all have higher upside among Houston's WRs for Week 10 and beyond.

free_agents.name: Kayshon Boutte
free_agents.outlook: Kayshon Boutte had four catches for 125 yards and two TDs in Week 9 against the Chargers, recording his best game in a Texans uniform. Prior to that outburst, Boutte was averaging under 28 receiving yards per game and hadn't scored a TD all season. He demonstrated that his ceiling is high enough to warrant a dart throw if you're desperate, but Boutte will be hard-pressed to repeat Week 9's production in Week 10 against the Browns since playing time remains hard to come by in a Texans WR room that also includes Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Xavier Hutchinson and Marvin Harrison. Boutte's breakout game against the Chargers came on just a 33% snap share.

free_agents.name: Nick Folk
free_agents.outlook: Nick Folk likely won't have many scoring opportunities during the Falcons' Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. Folk has struggled over the last two weeks, converting on just one of three field-goal tries while making both point-after attempts. On the season, he's made just 72% of his field-goal attempts (13 of 18) and 94% of his extra-points (17 of 18). Folk could have few scoring opportunities in Week 10, as the Falcons' offense as a whole has underperformed over the last two weeks, though Kansas City's defense has allowed 8.4 kicking points per game.

free_agents.name: Greg Dulcich
free_agents.outlook: Greg Dulcich will again have a favorable matchup when the Dolphins face the Colts in Week 10. He was presented with the best possible matchup in Week 9 against Detroit but managed only 14 yards on four targets and remains without a touchdown reception on the season as Malik Willis struggled under center before being placed on the IR. Indianapolis has allowed seven touchdowns to tight ends, including one in each of their last three games, but Dulcich has been held to 43 yards or fewer in six of eight outings and now has to develop a rapport with new QB Kyle McCord. Dulcich is out of the Week 10 mix despite the favorable matchup.

free_agents.name: Jalen Nailor
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Nailor remains an afterthought in the Raiders' passing attack, catching two of four targets for nine yards in a Week 9 loss to the 49ers. He logs fairly steady target volume, but aside from a 4-38-1 line in Week 8 against the Jets, Nailor has done little with his opportunities. The former Viking isn't likely to break out in Week 10 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Jordan Watkins
free_agents.outlook: Jordan Watkins may not get a chance to build upon a career-best performance for San Francisco in Week 10 against Dallas. Watkins caught all four of his targets for a career-high 86 yards and his first NFL touchdown in Week 9 against the Raiders, taking advantage of the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Watkins could again be featured versus the Cowboys if Evans and Samuel remain out, but the 49ers did add veteran Keenan Allen at the trade deadline, and he will almost certainly slot above Watkins on the depth chart. Watkins will carry an impressive average of 22.4 yards per reception into the contest against the Cowboys, who have given up 27 passing plays of 20-plus yards, eighth-most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Pierre Strong Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Pierre Strong could see an elevated role as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Strong logged eight carries for 22 yards and two catches for 11 yards in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, with MarShawn Lloyd and Josh Jacobs both dealing with injuries. The fourth-year ball carrier has served a change-of-pace role in his five appearances this season, but he could see even bigger usage if his position mates are inactive. Minnesota has ranked top 10 in fantasy points allowed to RBs this campaign.

free_agents.name: Drew Stevens
free_agents.outlook: Drew Stevens connected on two field goals as well as an extra point last game for the Commanders. Stevens has connected on multiple field goals in six of the last seven outings for Washington.  He has six made field goals in his last two games alone. In Week 10, Stevens will take on a Giants squad allowing 21.5 points per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jaylen Wright
free_agents.outlook: Jaylen Wright didn't factor into the Dolphins' backfield even before a quad injury cost him Week 9. He'll need to overcome that issue if he's to take aim at Indianapolis' vulnerable run defense in Week 10. Wright has just 19 total carries across his last four games, with Ollie Gordon dominating touches. The Colts are allowing 4.8 yards per carry and the fifth-most fantasy points per game to opposing rushers, but Wright hasn't been afforded enough chances to take advantage of those deficiencies.

free_agents.name: Ty Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Ty Johnson continues to flash in the Bills' passing game ahead of a Week 10 matchup with the Jets. He has only seven carries in six games but has brought in all 17 of his targets after snagging 24 balls in 17 games last season. While the volume is unlikely to be enough to merit fantasy consideration, the Jets have allowed four touchdown catches to opposing backs, the second-highest number in the league, which could allow Johnson to shine in Week 10.

free_agents.name: Chris Brooks
free_agents.outlook: Chris Brooks will look to make a return as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Brooks has been on IR with an ankle injury and while his required four games out were fulfilled ahead of Week 9 against the Patriots, Green Bay decided to not activate him. The fourth-year ball carrier will likely need to log at least one full practice this week if he hopes to take on a Minnesota defense that's ranked top 10 against fantasy running backs.

free_agents.name: Jauan Jennings
free_agents.outlook: Jauan Jennings will look to get healthy ahead of Minnesota's Week 10 matchup at Green Bay. Jennings sat out of a Week 9 loss to Buffalo with a calf injury, which he suffered during the previous Thursday's practice. If Jennings is able to play against the Packers, his production could improve with trade deadline acquisition Kirk Cousins under center, especially against a defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Dohnte Meyers
free_agents.outlook: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals host the division-rival Steelers in Week 10. He caught two of three targets for 47 yards and had a 16-yard carry during Cincinnati's 34-17 victory in Week 9. Meyers also returned four kicks for 100 yards and finished second on the team in receiving yardage. The Bengals like to get the ball in his hands, but with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins occupying the majority of Joe Burrow's attention, Meyers should remain on fantasy benches.

free_agents.name: Tre' Harris
free_agents.outlook: Tre' Harris tied his season high with seven targets in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, but he caught just three of them for six yards. The second-year wideout has hauled in more than three passes in a game only once in 2026, as Justin Herbert and the passing attack struggle with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel calling the shots. Ladd McConkey is now battling back trouble, but Harris is still unlikely to make a big impact in Week 10, even against a Ravens secondary that's tied for 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Carson Beck
free_agents.outlook: Carson Beck is expected to make his NFL debut as the Cardinals' starting quarterback in Week 10 against the Rams. Beck has yet to take a snap this season, but he's being pressed into a starting role after Jacoby Brissett was traded last weekend and after Gardner Minshew suffered a potentially season-ending elbow injury in Week 9. Beck will be working with an injury-riddled offense, as RB Jeremiyah Love is on IR due to an ankle injury and wideouts Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) are out for the season. It may be a tough opening assignment for Beck, as the Rams rank seventh in the league with an 82.3 QB rating allowed to passers.

free_agents.name: Gunnar Helm
free_agents.outlook: Gunnar Helm capitalized on a favorable matchup when Tennessee met the Bengals in Week 8, setting career highs with five catches for 76 yards on nine targets. He's likely to return to fantasy irrelevance in Week 10 against a Jacksonville defense that has held TEs to a league-low 250 yards through eight games. Prior to his career-best Week 8 outing, Helm had failed to exceed 28 receiving yards or score a TD in any game all season.

free_agents.name: Isaac TeSlaa
free_agents.outlook: Isaac TeSlaa will be a secondary option in Detroit's passing offense again in Week 10 against the Patriots. TeSlaa was quiet again in a gritty Week 9 win over Miami, reeling in one of two targets for just nine yards. After a solid stretch from Weeks 2 to 4, the second-year pass catcher has now recorded just two catches for 19 yards in his last four showings. Luckily, he'll face a New England defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Carson Wentz
free_agents.outlook: Carson Wentz will return to the bench in Week 10 as the Vikings play the Packers. The trade deadline acquisition of Kirk Cousins gives Minnesota a clear upgrade at QB, and Wentz will compete with Kyler Murray for the No. 2 role once Murray has put a hamstring injury behind him.

free_agents.name: Andy Borregales
free_agents.outlook: Andy Borregales remains void of a spike scoring week ahead of the Patriots' Week 10 matchup with the Lions. Borregales has just three games with multiple made field goals to date, limiting his ceiling and floor despite three or more PATs in six straight outings. Detroit is allowing the fourth fewest fantasy points to opposing kickers as opponents are routinely converting drives into touchdowns, suggesting Sunday can again be a busy yet low-scoring outing for Borregales.

free_agents.name: Oronde Gadsden
free_agents.outlook: Oronde Gadsden was held in check in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, catching two of three targets for 17 yards. The second-year tight end has struggled to fit into offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, and this season he has as many games with zero catches as he does with performances of more than three grabs. Overall, Gadsden has managed a 19-172-1 line on 29 targets over eight contests. He'll look to make a difference in Week 10 against a Ravens defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

free_agents.name: Reggie Virgil
free_agents.outlook: Reggie Virgil is among a group of Arizona wideouts who could be set for an increased opportunity in Week 10 against the Rams. Virgil has just three catches for 54 yards on 11 targets through five games this season, so he's been off the fantasy radar. However, Michael Wilson is expected to miss the remainder of the campaign due to a neck injury, as is Kendrick Bourne (tibia). That likely leaves Virgil vying for the Cardinals No. 1 wideout role alongside the likes of Simi Fehoko and Devin Duvernay. It won't be an easy test for Arizona's wideout corps against the Rams, who have given up just 17.9 fantasy points per game to the position, eighth-best in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Chris Bell
free_agents.outlook: Chris Bell has failed to gain traction in the Dolphins' limited passing game ahead of a Week 10 tilt against the Colts. Bell logged only one target in Week 9 despite a 58% snap share and has been held without a catch in half of his eight outings. Miami's passing game cannot sustain multiple relevant receivers, and Indianapolis is far more vulnerable to the run, likely preventing Bell from a long-awaited breakout.

free_agents.name: Zachariah Branch
free_agents.outlook: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will likely play a reserve role in Atlanta's wide receiver room if active for the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. Branch was unable to practice all of last week after sustaining a hamstring injury in the Week 8 loss to the Buccaneers, so he'll definitely need to make some progress to suit up Sunday. On the season, the rookie wideout has caught 10 of 12 targets for 64 yards and rushed once for eight yards, contributing primarily on special teams. If Branch plays in Week 10, he'll likely struggle against a Kansas City secondary that's allowed just 9.9 yards per completion this year.

free_agents.name: Chimere Dike
free_agents.outlook: Chimere Dike stepped up in Week 8 with five catches for 71 yards and a TD in the absence of Carnell Tate (shoulder). Tate is expected to return after Tennessee's Week 9 bye, which will likely bump Dike back to a bench role on offense against the Jaguars in Week 10. Dike can be ignored in standard fantasy formats but remains an elite option in leagues that reward return yards on special teams, as the 2025 fourth-round pick leads the NFL with 3,517 all-purpose yards since entering the league.

free_agents.name: Sione Vaki
free_agents.outlook: Sione Vaki will remain Detroit's secondary option at running back in Week 10 against New England. After a high-volume Week 8 performance against the Vikings, Vaki was quieter in Week 9 with three rushes for 14 yards and two catches for seven yards in Miami. The third-year ball carrier hasn't had the most elegant RB2 campaign behind Jahmyr Gibbs, but he has made the most of his opportunities. The Patriots have ranked a tough fifth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

free_agents.name: Kyle McCord
free_agents.outlook: Kyle McCord is slated to take over the helm for the Dolphins after starting QB Malik Willis was diagnosed with a core-muscle injury, sending him to the IR until at least Week 14. An impressive camp earned McCord the backup role, but he has yet to log any action this season. When he does, it will be on the road against a Colts defense vulnerable to the run, so expect McCord to spend most of Week 10 handing the ball off to Ollie Gordon, Mike Washington and perhaps Jaylen Wright (quad).

free_agents.name: Savion Williams
free_agents.outlook: Savion Williams will aim to stay involved as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Williams put together his best performance of the season in a Week 9 win over New England, logging six total touches for 38 yards, along with a receiving touchdown. The second-year gadget receiver has operated as Green Bay's clear WR3 after returning from IR in Week 6. He'll face a Minnesota defense that's ranked top five in points allowed to fantasy WRs this campaign.

free_agents.name: Laquon Treadwell
free_agents.outlook: Laquon Treadwell finished without a catch in the Colts' Week 9 loss to Dallas. He continues to earn playing time in Indianapolis' weak wide receiver room, exceeding a 70% snap share in each of the past eight games. The journeyman WR hasn't made the most of his opportunities, with just 16 catches for 215 yards and no TDs through nine games, averaging just 24 yards per game. Even with Josh Downs and Keenan Allen having been traded away, Treadwell remains off the fantasy radar in Week 10 against Miami's stingy secondary.

free_agents.name: KaVontae Turpin
free_agents.outlook: KaVontae Turpin has missed each of the last three games for Dallas due to a rib ailment. His status remains up in the air for Week 10 versus the 49ers. If Turpin does suit up, his opportunities will likely be limited against a Niners defense allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Charlie Smyth
free_agents.outlook: Charlie Smyth is expected to have some solid scoring opportunities during the Saints' Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Smyth made his regular-season debut after being elevated to the active roster ahead of the Week 9 win over the Browns. He converted on three of four field-goal tries and made both point-after attempts, likely solidifying himself as the Saints' top kicker again in Week 10. He'll likely have scoring chances in Week 10 as well, with the Panthers' defense allowing 7.4 kicking points per game this season.

free_agents.name: Darnell Mooney
free_agents.outlook: Darnell Mooney collected a season-high 54 receiving yards last game for the Giants. However, he also picked up a chest injury and is listed as questionable for the Week 10 tilt versus the Commanders. If Mooney can suit up, he will look to take advantage of a porous Washington secondary. The Commanders are allowing 240 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, Washington has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 25th in the league.

free_agents.name: Gardner Minshew II
free_agents.outlook: Gardner Minshew is expected to miss Arizona's Week 10 clash against the Rams due to an elbow injury. As a result, rookie Carson Beck is expected to take over as the Cardinals' starting quarterback.
